karmapa-16.bio: Head of the Karma Kagyu who re-established the school in exile at Rumtek and brought it to the West.

karmapa-17.bio: Recognised as the 17th Karmapa by the Dalai Lama and most Kagyu authorities; a rival candidate also exists.

akong-rinpoche.bio: Co-founder and long-time abbot of Samye Ling in Scotland.

chogyam-trungpa.bio: Tibetan teacher who co-founded Samye Ling, then founded Naropa University and Shambhala in North America.

pema-chodron.bio: American nun and author, a student of Chögyam Trungpa, resident teacher at Gampo Abbey.

chokyi-nyima-rinpoche.bio: Eldest son of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in Boudha.

padmasambhava.bio: Eighth-century tantric master credited with establishing Buddhism in Tibet.

gyokujun-so-on.bio: Soto priest who ordained Shunryu Suzuki and gave him dharma transmission.

kishizawa-ian.bio: Soto scholar-teacher who further trained Shunryu Suzuki in Dogen's Shobogenzo.

richard-baker.bio: Shunryu Suzuki's dharma heir and second abbot of San Francisco Zen Center.

kodo-sawaki.bio: Itinerant Soto master who stressed zazen alone ('homeless Kodo'); teacher of Kosho Uchiyama.

gudo-nishijima.bio: Japanese Zen teacher and Shobogenzo translator, Brad Warner's teacher.

img.artist: Permission granted by James M. Cohen, Attorney at Law

hakuun-yasutani.bio: Founder of the Sanbo Kyodan, who taught Philip Kapleau and Taizan Maezumi.

taizan-maezumi.bio: Founder of the Zen Center of Los Angeles; many American teachers are his heirs.

bernie-glassman.bio: Maezumi's first heir, founder of the Zen Peacemakers and teacher of Joan Halifax.

img.artist: Stephanie Young Merzel from Salt Lake City, Utah, USA

john-daido-loori.bio: Maezumi heir who founded Zen Mountain Monastery.

philip-kapleau.bio: Author of The Three Pillars of Zen and founder of the Rochester Zen Center.

img.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Mind meal~commonswiki assumed

eido-shimano.bio: Rinzai teacher who founded Dai Bosatsu Zendo; he resigned in 2010 after misconduct revelations.

bodhidharma.bio: Legendary Indian monk honoured as the first patriarch of Chan.

huineng.bio: Sixth Chan patriarch, figure of the Platform Sutra.

thich-chan-that.bio: Abbot of Tu Hieu Temple and Thich Nhat Hanh's root teacher.

annamalai-swami.bio: Ramana Maharshi's attendant and builder who later taught self-enquiry from his small ashram.

gangaji.bio: American teacher of self-enquiry who met Papaji in 1990.

bhausaheb-maharaj.bio: Founder of the Inchegeri lineage at Inchgiri; teacher of Siddharameshwar.

swami-ram-kashmir.bio: Kashmiri Shaiva master of the late nineteenth century, root of Lakshmanjoo's lineage.

swami-mahtab-kak.bio: Disciple of Swami Ram and teacher of Swami Lakshmanjoo.

john-hughes.bio: Long-time student of Lakshmanjoo who recorded and publishes his teachings.

alexis-sanderson.bio: Oxford Indologist of Shaiva tantra who read texts with Lakshmanjoo.

kshemaraja.bio: Abhinavagupta's leading disciple, author of the Pratyabhijnahrdayam.

vasugupta.bio: Ninth-century sage to whom the Shiva Sutras were revealed.

bhagawan-nityananda.bio: Avadhuta saint of Ganeshpuri and guru of Muktananda.

muktananda.bio: Founder of Siddha Yoga, who drew on Kashmir Shaiva texts.

swami-chinmayananda.bio: Vedanta teacher who founded Chinmaya Mission and taught Swami Dayananda.

swami-brahmananda.bio: Direct disciple of Ramakrishna and first president of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission.

thomas-merton.bio: Trappist monk of Gethsemani and writer on contemplation and interfaith dialogue.

thomas-keating.bio: Trappist abbot who helped develop Centering Prayer.

brother-roger.bio: Swiss founder of the ecumenical Taizé Community.

bede-griffiths.bio: English Benedictine who led Shantivanam ashram and joined Christian and Hindu contemplation.

abhishiktananda.bio: French Benedictine who co-founded Shantivanam and was transformed by meeting Ramana.

alexander-von-rospatt.bio: UC Berkeley Buddhologist; co-chair of Christopher Wallis's dissertation committee.

amitabh-trika-school.bio: Teacher of the Trika School of Tantra, which posts short teachings and guided meditations on Kashmir Shaivism; lineage not independently verified.

amritananda.bio: Nuclear physicist (Dr Nishtala Prahlada Sastry, 23 years at TIFR Mumbai) who became a Śrī Vidyā guru and founded the Devipuram temple near Visakhapatnam, known for opening Śrī Vidyā initiation and Śrī Chakra worship to all.

andre-padoux.bio: French diplomat turned CNRS scholar of tantric mantra and speech (Vāc); read Abhinavagupta with Lakshmanjoo in Srinagar in 1958–59.

ben-williams.bio: Scholar-practitioner of Śaiva tantra and Abhinavagupta; frequent guest on yoga-studies podcasts.

bettina-baumer.bio: Austrian-born Indologist living in Varanasi; a student of Swami Lakshmanjoo who lectures on the Vijñāna Bhairava, Śiva Sūtras, Spanda and Netra Tantra and on Abhinavagupta's aesthetics.

bjarne-wernicke-olesen.bio: Danish scholar of Śākta and Kubjikā traditions.

bodhinatha-veylanswami.bio: Head of Kauai's Hindu Monastery (Kauai Aadheenam) and publisher of Hinduism Today; successor of Sivaya Subramuniyaswami in the Nandinatha Sampradaya, teaching a monistic Śaiva Siddhānta.

csaba-kiss.bio: Budapest (ELTE) Indologist; Oxford doctorate on the Matsyendrasaṃhitā, editor of Brahmayāmala volume II.

daniel-odier.bio: French writer and teacher of Kashmiri Tantra (Spanda, Kālī practice, Tāṇḍava) and Chan; many uploads are in French, only English ones are kept.

daniela-bevilacqua.bio: Ethnographer of Hindu ascetics on the Haṭha Yoga Project.

david-gordon-white.bio: UCSB historian of religions (PhD Chicago 1988) known for The Alchemical Body, Kiss of the Yoginī and Sinister Yogis.

dominic-goodall.bio: Sanskritist at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (head of its Pondicherry centre 2002–2011); editor of early Śaiva Siddhānta texts such as the Kiraṇavṛtti and the Niśvāsatattvasaṃhitā.

douglas-brooks.bio: Professor of religion at the University of Rochester (PhD Harvard) and founder of the Rajanaka teaching, rooted in South Indian Śrī Vidyā as learned from his teacher Gopala Aiyar Sundaramoorthy.

edwin-bryant.bio: Rutgers scholar of the Yoga Sūtras and Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

elizabeth-de-michelis.bio: Cambridge scholar of modern yoga (A History of Modern Yoga); supervised Mark Singleton.

eric-baret.bio: French teacher in the line of Jean Klein who presents Kashmir Shaivism as a non-dual, body-based listening.

gavin-flood.bio: Oxford scholar of Hinduism and comparative religion; author of The Tantric Body and studies of the Netra Tantra and Śaiva theology.

gopala-aiyar-sundaramoorthy.bio: Sanskrit professor at Madurai-Kamaraj University and teacher of Douglas Brooks; source of the Rajanaka teaching.

gorakhnath.bio: Founder-figure of the Nāth yogīs, credited with haṭha texts such as the Amaraugha.

harunaga-isaacson.bio: Professor of Classical Indology at Hamburg, specialist in Indian Vajrayāna Buddhism and its links with tantric Śaivism.

igor-kufayev.bio: Russian-born, Europe-based teacher whose darshans and courses draw heavily on Kashmir Shaivism (Trika, Krama, Spanda) and on kundalini as the process of awakening.

jaideva-singh.bio: Indian scholar whose English translations of the Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam, Śiva Sūtras, Spanda Kārikās and Vijñāna Bhairava made Kashmir Shaivism widely readable; worked closely with Lakshmanjoo.

james-mallinson.bio: Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and leader of the Haṭha Yoga Project; edited the Khecarīvidyā, Dattātreyayogaśāstra and Amṛtasiddhi; also an initiated Rāmānandī mahant.

jason-birch.bio: Historian of medieval yoga on the Haṭha Yoga Project; editor of the Amanaska, Amaraugha and Yogacintāmaṇi.

judit-torzsok.bio: Professor of Śaiva Studies at the EPHE, Paris; works on early Śākta tantras such as the Siddhayogeśvarīmata and on yoginī cults.

kavitha-chinnaiyan.bio: Cardiologist and teacher of Śrī Vidyā and Advaita (Svatantra Institute).

lakulisha.bio: Traditional founder of the Pāśupata ascetic order, the earliest named Śaiva movement (Atimārga).

lilian-silburn.bio: French CNRS Indologist who studied Trika with Lakshmanjoo from 1949 and published French translations of the Vijñāna Bhairava, Śiva Sūtras and (with Padoux) the Tantrāloka.

loriliai-biernacki.bio: Scholar of Hindu tantra (University of Colorado Boulder) writing on women in tantra, Abhinavagupta, wonder and new materialism.

lorin-roche.bio: Meditation teacher known for The Radiance Sutras, a free poetic rendering of the Vijñāna Bhairava.

louis-renou.bio: French Vedic scholar who directed Lilian Silburn's thesis and taught André Padoux Sanskrit.

mark-dyczkowski.bio: English Indologist and sitarist in Varanasi, initiated by Lakshmanjoo in 1976; translator of the Spanda texts, the 11-volume Tantrāloka and the Manthānabhairava Tantra.

mark-singleton.bio: Scholar of modern and premodern yoga (Yoga Body, Roots of Yoga with Mallinson); senior researcher on the Haṭha Yoga Project.

mary-reilly-nichols.bio: Yoga and meditation teacher formed in Siddha Yoga who teaches Kashmir Shaivism.

matsyendranatha.bio: Legendary founder of the Kaula yoginī cult and first guru of the Nāth lineage.

om-swami.bio: Indian monk and author who teaches mantra sādhana and Śrī Vidyā; many talks are in Hindi, so only English uploads were kept.

paul-muller-ortega.bio: Scholar of Indian religions (PhD, University of California) who taught at Michigan State and Rochester for 25 years, then founded Blue Throat Yoga (2006) to teach Neelakantha Meditation from the Śaiva–Śākta tradition of Kashmir.

rajarshi-nandy.bio: Indian upāsaka of Bhairava, Kālī and Kāmākhyā who founded the Kamakhya Bhairava Upasaka Foundation (KBUF); speaks in English, sometimes mixed with Hindi, on Shākta sādhana.

rajmani-tigunait.bio: Spiritual head of the Himalayan Institute and successor of Swami Rama; Sanskritist who teaches Śrī Vidyā, the Śrī Sūkta and tantric mantra practice.

richard-gombrich.bio: Oxford Indologist and Buddhologist; supervised Mark Dyczkowski's doctorate.

robert-goldman.bio: UC Berkeley Sanskritist; co-chair of Christopher Wallis's dissertation committee.

sadhguru.bio: Founder of the Isha Foundation; consecrated the Linga Bhairavi goddess form at Coimbatore and teaches Bhairavi Sadhana as a devotional practice open to lay people.

sally-kempton.bio: Journalist turned monastic in Swami Muktananda's Siddha Yoga (met Muktananda in 1974; initiated as Swami Durgananda in 1982); later an independent teacher of meditation, Kashmir Shaivism and goddess practice (Awakening Shakti, Meditation for the Love of It).

seth-powell.bio: Historian of yoga and founder of the Yogic Studies platform and podcast.

shaman-hatley.bio: Scholar of early tantric Śaivism and yoginī cults (UMass Boston); editor of the Brahmayāmala.

shambhavi-sarasvati.bio: Spiritual director of Jaya Kula in Portland, Oregon, teaching Trika Shaivism alongside Tibetan Dzogchen; Anandamayi Ma is her root guru.

sivaya-subramuniyaswami.bio: American-born founder of Kauai's Hindu Monastery and Himalayan Academy, initiated by Yogaswami of Jaffna; author of Dancing with Siva and Merging with Siva.

somadeva-vasudeva.bio: Professor at Kyoto University; his Oxford doctorate edited the yoga chapters of the Mālinīvijayottaratantra; works on esoteric Śaiva yoga and Sanskrit poetics.

somananda.bio: Author of the Śivadṛṣṭi, first philosophical statement of non-dual Śaivism in Kashmir; teacher of Utpaladeva.

sravana-borkataky-varma.bio: Scholar of Śākta tantra in Assam and of women practitioners.

sthaneshwar-timalsina.bio: Nepali-born scholar-practitioner (San Diego State University) who teaches Śākta and Śaiva tantra through his Vimarsha Foundation.

swami-khecaranatha.bio: American teacher in the line of Swami Rudrananda (Rudi) who teaches Trika Shaivism and kundalini practice through his Heart of Consciousness community.

swami-rama.bio: Founder of the Himalayan Institute and teacher of Pandit Rajmani Tigunait.

swami-rudrananda.bio: American teacher of kundalini practice, root of Swami Khecaranatha's line.

swami-shankarananda.bio: Disciple of Swami Muktananda who founded the Shiva Ashram near Melbourne; teaches Kashmir Shaivism and his own self-inquiry method, the Shiva Process.

tilmann-vetter.bio: Leiden Indologist; supervised Harunaga Isaacson's doctorate.

utpaladeva.bio: Author of the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā, the founding text of the Recognition (Pratyabhijñā) school; student of Somānanda.

yamajit.bio: Teacher at the Tridevi Chamunda Mandir who streams long satsangs on the twelve Kālīs of the Krama, the Mātṛkās, the 64 Yoginīs and Vijñāna Bhairava meditations.

yogaswami.bio: Sri Lankan Tamil Śaiva sage, guru of Sivaya Subramuniyaswami.

ajahn-brahmali.bio: Norwegian-born monk trained under Ajahn Brahm at Bodhinyana; teaches the early suttas and Vinaya closely, often co-teaching sutta courses with Bhante Sujato.

bhante-sujato.bio: Australian monk ordained in the Ajahn Chah tradition; founder of Santi Forest Monastery and co-founder of SuttaCentral, where he has published free English translations of the four main Nikāyas.

texts.title: SuttaCentral translations (Sujato; Brahmali Vinaya)

ajahn-hasapanna.bio: Monk of the Bodhinyana / BSWA community in Western Australia, a student of Ajahn Brahm.

ajahn-nyaniko.bio: Senior monk at Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition; gives many of the monastery's evening and retreat talks.

ajahn-karunadhammo.bio: American monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition and former abbot of Abhayagiri.

ajahn-cunda.bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

ajahn-sudhiro.bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

ajahn-ahimsako.bio: Monk of Cittaviveka (Chithurst) Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

ajahn-karuniko.bio: Senior monk at Cittaviveka (Chithurst) in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

ajahn-sona.bio: Canadian monk and co-founder of Birken Forest Monastery in British Columbia, in the Thai forest tradition; known for practical talks on jhāna and daily life.

ajahn-anan.bio: Thai monk who ordained under Ajahn Chah in 1975 and founded Wat Marp Jan in Rayong; teaches weekly in Thai with English translation.

ajahn-kalyano.bio: Australian monk, a long-time student and translator of Ajahn Anan; abbot of Buddha Bodhivana Monastery near Melbourne.

ajahn-chandako.bio: American-born monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition; abbot of Vimutti Buddhist Monastery in New Zealand.

sayadaw-u-silananda.bio: Burmese scholar-monk trained in the Mahasi tradition; founded the Theravada Buddhist Society of America and taught Abhidhamma and satipaṭṭhāna in California.

sayadaw-u-thuzana.bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

sayadaw-u-nandasiri.bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

bhikkhu-analayo.bio: German-born monk and scholar ordained in Sri Lanka; specialist in comparative study of the Pāli Nikāyas and Chinese Āgamas, and author of widely used books on satipaṭṭhāna.

swami-pavitrananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order who led the Vedanta Society of New York from 1951; heard here in archival recordings.

swami-tathagatananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and long-time head of the Vedanta Society of New York; heard here in archival recordings.

swami-dhyanayogananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

swami-medhananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and philosopher (Ayon Maharaj), author of studies of Ramakrishna's and Vivekananda's philosophy.

pravrajika-vrajaprana.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent (Vedanta Society of Southern California) and author of books on Vedanta.

pravrajika-krishnaprana.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent, Vedanta Society of Southern California.

swami-tyagananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, head of the Ramakrishna Vedanta Society of Boston and Hindu chaplain at Harvard and MIT.

swami-chetanananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, minister of the Vedanta Society of St. Louis and author of histories of Ramakrishna's disciples.

swami-shivarchanananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of St. Louis.

swami-ishatmananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vivekananda Vedanta Society of Chicago.

swami-tejomayananda.bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and former head of the Chinmaya Mission worldwide.

swami-swaroopananda-chinmaya.bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and current global head of the Chinmaya Mission.

swamini-svatmavidyananda.bio: Traditional teacher of Vedānta in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

swami-tattvavidananda.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati teaching Vedānta and Sanskrit.

swami-viditatmananda.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati, long associated with the Arsha Vidya Gurukulam.

radhanath-swami.bio: American-born Gaudiya Vaishnava teacher in ISKCON, a disciple of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, and author of "The Journey Home".

swami-niranjanananda.bio: Successor of Swami Satyananda Saraswati and long-time head of the Bihar School of Yoga in Munger.

swami-swaroopananda-sivananda.bio: Senior acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

swami-sitaramananda.bio: Acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Farm in California, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

swami-paramananda-sivananda.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Paramananda, 1884–1940).

swami-shambhudevananda.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

swami-brahmananda-sivananda.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Brahmananda).

ajahn-dtun.bio: Thai monk ordained at Wat Nong Pah Pong with Ajahn Chah as preceptor (1978); trained with Ajahn Piak and Ajahn Anan and founded Wat Boonyawad in Chonburi.

texts.title: The Autobiography and Dhamma Teachings of Ajahn Dtun

alexander-wynne.bio: British scholar of early Buddhism; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich, author of "The Origin of Buddhist Meditation", and an editor of the Journal of the OCBS.

rupert-gethin.bio: British scholar of the Nikāyas and Abhidhamma, emeritus professor at Bristol and president of the Pali Text Society; PhD at Manchester under Lance Cousins.

steven-collins.bio: British scholar of Pāli Buddhism at Chicago, author of "Selfless Persons" and "Nirvana and Other Buddhist Felicities"; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich.

jeffery-long.bio: American scholar of Hindu and Jain traditions at Elizabethtown College, closely associated with the Vedanta Societies.

tkv-desikachar.bio: Son and student of T. Krishnamacharya; founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai and taught yoga adapted to the individual.

wendy-doniger.bio: American Indologist at the University of Chicago, translator of Sanskrit texts and author of "The Hindus: An Alternative History".

nick-sutton.bio: Scholar of the Mahābhārata and Bhagavad Gītā who teaches the OCHS online courses.

lance-cousins.bio: British scholar of Pāli and Abhidhamma (Manchester, Oxford) and samatha meditation teacher; supervised Rupert Gethin.

paul-williams.bio: British scholar of Mahāyāna Buddhism at Bristol; taught Alexander Wynne and introduced Steven Collins to Gombrich.

katukurunde-nanananda.bio: Sri Lankan forest monk and author of "Concept and Reality" and the "Nibbāna – The Mind Stilled" sermons.

balangoda-ananda-maitreya.bio: Sri Lankan scholar-monk who was Bhikkhu Bodhi's preceptor.

ajahn-piak.bio: Thai disciple of Ajahn Chah and abbot of Wat Pah Cittabhavana; Ajahn Dtun and Ajahn Anan trained alongside him.

tapovan-maharaj.bio: Himalayan Vedānta master at Uttarkashi; Swami Chinmayananda's teacher.

swami-vishnudevananda.bio: Disciple of Swami Sivananda who founded the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

swami-satyananda.bio: Disciple of Swami Sivananda who founded the Bihar School of Yoga (1963).

krishnamacharya.bio: South Indian yoga teacher whose students (Desikachar, Iyengar, Pattabhi Jois, Indra Devi) shaped modern postural yoga.

bks-iyengar.bio: Student and brother-in-law of Krishnamacharya; founder of Iyengar Yoga.

pattabhi-jois.bio: Student of Krishnamacharya; founder of Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga in Mysore.

chaitanya-mahaprabhu.bio: Bengali saint whose ecstatic Krishna devotion founded the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition.

bhaktisiddhanta.bio: Founder of the Gaudiya Math and guru of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.

bhaktivedanta-swami-prabhupada.bio: Founder of ISKCON (1966), who brought Gaudiya Vaishnavism to the West.

daniel-ingalls.bio: Harvard Sanskritist; supervised Wendy Doniger's Harvard PhD.

swami-paramarthananda.bio: Chennai-based disciple of Swami Dayananda, known for systematic English Vedānta classes (no official YouTube channel found).

dzogchen-ponlop.bio: Kagyu and Nyingma lama, founder of Nalandabodhi, who presents mind training and the "mindful gap" to modern audiences with humour and an interest in art and popular culture.

ringu-tulku.bio: Karma Kagyu lama and scholar of the Rimé movement, former professor of Tibetan studies in Sikkim, who founded Bodhicharya and teaches in a light, accessible style.

tenzin-wangyal.bio: Bön lama trained at Menri under Lopön Tenzin Namdak, founder of Ligmincha International, who teaches Bön Dzogchen, dream yoga and the healing practices of sound and breath.

valerie-forstman.bio: Associate Zen Master of the Sanbo Zen lineage and guiding teacher of Mountain Cloud Zen Center, first a student of Ruben Habito.

chigan-roshi.bio: Rinzai Zen teacher with the Zen Studies Society who gives teisho on koan collections at Dai Bosatsu Zendo and New York Zendo.

jeffrey-hopkins.bio: Scholar and translator of Gelug Madhyamaka and tantra, founder of the Tibetan Buddhist studies doctoral programme at the University of Virginia and the Dalai Lama's chief English interpreter 1979–89.

lama-jampa-thaye.bio: British-born lama authorised in the Sakya and Karma Kagyu traditions by Karma Thinley Rinpoche, founder of the Dechen community and a scholar of Tibetan Buddhism.

kwan-um-school.n: Kwan Um School of Zen (various Zen Masters)
kwan-um-school.bio: The Kwan Um School of Zen, the international Korean Seon school founded by Zen Master Seung Sahn; the channel collects short talks by many of its Zen Masters.

tendai-buddhist-institute.bio: Tendai Buddhist Institute in New York state, the American branch of Japanese Tendai; its weekly Wednesday talks cover Tiantai/Tendai doctrine and practice.

shingon-foundation.n: Foundation for Shingon Buddhism (classes and podcast)
shingon-foundation.bio: Foundation for Shingon Buddhism, which shares Shingon esoteric Buddhism, its texts and Koyasan culture in English.

dzongsar-khyentse.bio: Bhutanese Rimé lama of the Sakya and Nyingma lines, recognised as an incarnation of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo; filmmaker, author and founder of Siddhartha's Intent and Khyentse Foundation.

alan-wallace.bio: American scholar-practitioner ordained by the Dalai Lama and trained by Geshe Rabten, later a Stanford PhD, who teaches shamatha and Dzogchen and argues for a "contemplative science" of mind.

khentrul-rinpoche.bio: Shar Khentrul Jamphel Lodrö, a Jonang master trained in a non-sectarian (Rimé) way, who teaches Kalachakra and the shentong "other-emptiness" view through Dzokden.

robert-thurman.bio: American scholar and translator, the first Westerner ordained a Tibetan Buddhist monk, Jey Tsong Khapa Professor at Columbia and co-founder of Tibet House US; died in June 2026.

sheng-yen.bio: Taiwanese Chan master of the Linji and Caodong lines and founder of Dharma Drum Mountain, who revived Chan practice and taught in the West; his Great Dharma Drum TV series answers short questions.

dzigar-kongtrul.bio: Nyingma lama, son of Neten Chokling Rinpoche and former professor at Naropa, founder of Mangala Shri Bhuti, and teacher of Pema Chödrön.

hokuto-sensei.bio: Rinzai Zen priest with the Zen Studies Society (Hokuto Osho) who gives Dharma talks on the Record of Linji.

anne-klein.bio: Professor of Religious Studies at Rice University and, as Lama Rigzin Drolma, co-founder of Dawn Mountain in Houston, teaching Nyingma Dzogchen.

thupten-jinpa.bio: Former Gelug monk with a Geshe Lharampa degree and a Cambridge PhD, principal English translator to the Dalai Lama since 1985, Tsongkhapa biographer and author of the Compassion Cultivation Training programme.

jundo-cohen.bio: American Soto Zen priest living in Japan, Dharma heir of Gudo Wafu Nishijima and founder of the online Treeleaf Zendo.

tsultrim-allione.bio: American teacher, one of the first Western women ordained in Tibetan Buddhism (1970), founder of Tara Mandala and author of Women of Wisdom and Feeding Your Demons, a modern adaptation of Chöd.

chozen-bays.bio: Jan Chozen Bays, Dharma heir of Taizan Maezumi, paediatrician and co-abbot of Great Vow Zen Monastery in Oregon.

meian-elbert.bio: Abbess of Shasta Abbey in the Order of Buddhist Contemplatives founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

jiryu-rutschman-byler.bio: Soto Zen priest and former abbot of Green Gulch Farm, San Francisco Zen Center.

anam-thubten.bio: Tibetan teacher trained in the Nyingma tradition who leads the Dharmata Foundation in California and teaches a direct, non-sectarian approach to awakening.

phakchok-rinpoche.bio: Nyingma and Kagyu lineage holder, grandson of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and founder of the Samye Institute.

guo-gu.bio: Guo Gu (Jimmy Yu), Dharma heir of Master Sheng Yen and professor of religion at Florida State University, who teaches silent illumination and huatou at the Tallahassee Chan Center.

david-germano.bio: Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia, a historian of the Great Perfection (Dzogchen) and founder of the Tibetan and Himalayan Library and UVA's Contemplative Sciences Center.

barry-magid.bio: Psychiatrist and Dharma heir of Charlotte Joko Beck who founded Ordinary Mind Zendo in New York.

elizabeth-mattis-namgyel.bio: American teacher in the Nyingma line of Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, author of The Power of an Open Question, who explores Madhyamaka "not knowing" in daily life.

lama-lena.bio: American teacher (Yeshe Kaytup) of Dzogchen and Mahamudra, a long-time student of Wangdor Rinpoche, known for informal, precise "direct mind perception" teachings streamed from many cities.

shenpen-hookham.bio: British Kagyu and Nyingma teacher, Oxford DPhil on shentong buddha-nature, founder of the Awakened Heart Sangha.

phap-hai.bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Hải), Dharma teacher in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition.

kokyo-henkel.bio: Soto Zen priest from the San Francisco Zen Center lineage, guiding teacher of Santa Cruz Zen Center, with a strong interest in buddha-nature texts.

jetsunma-tenzin-palmo.bio: British-born Drukpa Kagyu nun who spent twelve years in a Himalayan cave and founded Dongyu Gatsal Ling nunnery.

tulku-thondup.bio: Nyingma scholar trained at Dodrupchen monastery, former visiting scholar at Harvard, author of books on healing, the Longchen Nyingthig and the hidden treasure (terma) tradition.

lama-rod-owens.bio: Black, queer Kagyu lama who completed a three-year retreat under Lama Norlha Rinpoche; teaches on anger, healing and collective liberation and leads Medicine Buddha practice online.

menri-trizin.bio: The 34th Menri Trizin, abbot of Menri Monastery in Dolanji and spiritual head of the Bön tradition, successor to Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (d. 2017).

willa-blythe-baker.bio: Kagyu lineage holder authorised after two three-year retreats, Harvard PhD (2013) and founder of Natural Dharma Fellowship and Wonderwell Mountain Refuge; teaches somatic mindfulness and Mahamudra.

jan-willis.bio: Professor emerita of religion at Wesleyan and long-time student of Lama Thubten Yeshe, who writes on Tibetan hagiography, women and race in Buddhism.

reb-anderson.bio: Senior Dharma teacher at San Francisco Zen Center, ordained by Shunryu Suzuki, known for close readings of Dogen and the bodhisattva precepts.

paul-swanson.bio: Scholar and translator of Tiantai at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture, translator of Zhiyi's Mohe zhiguan (Clear Serenity, Quiet Insight).

donald-lopez.bio: Arthur E. Link Distinguished University Professor at Michigan, a historian of Tibetan Buddhism and of the Western reception of Buddhism.

dae-bong.bio: American Zen Master in Seung Sahn's Kwan Um School, guiding teacher at Hwagyesa International Zen Center in Seoul.

duncan-williams.bio: Soto Zen priest and professor at the University of Southern California, author of American Sutra on Japanese American Buddhists in wartime incarceration.

alexander-berzin.bio: American scholar-translator who studied under Tsenzhab Serkong Rinpoche and the Dalai Lama in Dharamsala and created the Berzin Archives (now Study Buddhism), a large free library of Gelug and comparative teachings.

phap-huu.bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Hữu), long-time attendant of Thich Nhat Hanh and abbot of Upper Hamlet.

robert-sharf.bio: D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor of Buddhist Studies at UC Berkeley, a historian of Chan and Japanese Buddhism and a critic of "meditative experience" rhetoric.

garchen-rinpoche.bio: Drikung Kagyu master who spent some twenty years in Chinese labour camps, where he trained under Khenpo Münsel; teaches love and compassion as the heart of Mahamudra through the Garchen Buddhist Institute in Arizona.

sam-van-schaik.bio: English Tibetologist at the British Library, author of Tibet: A History, Tibetan Zen and The Spirit of Zen, who works on Dunhuang manuscripts and early Dzogchen.

brook-ziporyn.bio: Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago Divinity School, philosopher of Tiantai Buddhism and Zhuangzi.

geoffrey-samuel.bio: Anthropologist of Tibetan religion, emeritus professor at Cardiff, author of Civilized Shamans and The Origins of Yoga and Tantra.

bernard-faure.bio: French historian of Chan/Zen and esoteric Buddhism, emeritus at Columbia and Stanford, trained under Yanagida Seizan in Kyoto.

jacob-dalton.bio: Khyentse Foundation Distinguished Professor of Tibetan Buddhism at UC Berkeley, a historian of tantric ritual, the Nyingma school and the Dunhuang manuscripts.

phap-linh.bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Linh), Dharma teacher and musician in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition.

ruben-habito.bio: Filipino former Jesuit, Sanbo Zen teacher authorised in 1988 and founder of Maria Kannon Zen Center in Dallas.

jose-cabezon.bio: Dalai Lama Professor emeritus at UC Santa Barbara and former monk of Sera, who writes on Gelug and Nyingma philosophy, Sera monastery and Buddhist sexual ethics.

asanga-vajra.bio: Sakya lama of the Phuntsok Phodrang line who teaches at Sakya Monastery of Tibetan Buddhism in Seattle.

sakya-trizin.bio: Ngawang Kunga, 41st Sakya Trizin, head of the Sakya school for over five decades and now known as Sakya Trichen.

chan-duc.bio: Sister Chân Đức (Annabel Laity), senior English-born Dharma teacher of Plum Village.

seung-sahn.bio: Korean Seon master of the Jogye order who founded the Kwan Um School of Zen and taught "only don't know".

janet-gyatso.bio: Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard, a scholar of Tibetan visionary autobiography, medicine and gender.

steven-heine.bio: Scholar of Dogen and Zen koans at Florida International University.

taigen-leighton.bio: Soto Zen priest and Dharma heir of Tenshin Reb Anderson, translator of Dogen and Hongzhi, guiding teacher of Ancient Dragon Zen Gate in Chicago.

dosho-port.bio: Soto Zen teacher in the Dainin Katagiri line who hosts interviews with Zen teachers.

kenneth-tanaka.bio: Shin Buddhist priest and scholar, professor emeritus at Musashino University, writing on Pure Land thought and Buddhism in America.

dennis-hirota.bio: Scholar and translator of Shinran, head translator of the Collected Works of Shinran.

peter-gregory.bio: Scholar of Chinese Buddhism, author of Tsung-mi and the Sinification of Buddhism, a central study of Huayan and Chan.

richard-payne.bio: Scholar of Shingon ritual and tantric Buddhism, long-time dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies in Berkeley.

john-mcrae.bio: Historian of early Chinese Chan, author of The Northern School and Seeing through Zen, trained by Stanley Weinstein and Yanagida Seizan.

charles-jones.bio: Scholar of Chinese Pure Land and Taiwanese Buddhism at the Catholic University of America, author of Pure Land: History, Tradition, and Practice.

karl-brunnholzl.bio: German physician-turned-scholar and translator of Kagyu texts on Madhyamaka, Mahamudra and buddha-nature.

khenpo-sodargye.bio: Nyingma scholar from Larung Gar in eastern Tibet who teaches widely in Chinese.

chan-khong.bio: Vietnamese nun and social worker, Thich Nhat Hanh's closest collaborator in relief work and co-founder of Plum Village.

bodhin-kjolhede.bio: Abbot of the Rochester Zen Center and Dharma heir of Philip Kapleau.

mark-blum.bio: Scholar of Japanese Pure Land Buddhism at UC Berkeley and translator of Honen and the Nirvana Sutra.

griffith-foulk.bio: Scholar of Chan and Zen monastic institutions at Sarah Lawrence College and co-editor of the Soto Zen Text Project.

laurence-freeman.bio: Benedictine monk, student and successor of John Main, and director of the World Community for Christian Meditation.

iain-mcgilchrist.bio: Psychiatrist and philosopher, author of The Master and His Emissary and The Matter with Things, on the hemispheres and the sacred.

bernardo-kastrup.bio: Philosopher and computer engineer who argues for analytic idealism, the view that reality is fundamentally mental.

arthur-green.bio: Scholar of Hasidism and neo-Hasidic theologian; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis, founding dean of Hebrew College's rabbinical school.

pir-zia-inayat-khan.bio: Head of the Inayatiyya since 2004, grandson of Hazrat Inayat Khan and founder of Suluk Academy; PhD in religion from Duke.

omid-safi.bio: Duke University scholar of Islam who teaches Rumi, radical love and Sufi practice through his own courses and talks.

hisham-kabbani.bio: Lebanese-American Naqshbandi-Haqqani shaykh, deputy and son-in-law of Shaykh Nazim, who founded the order's centres in North America.

nour-kabbani.bio: Naqshbandi teacher, son and successor of Shaykh Hisham Kabbani and grandson of Shaykh Nazim.

baraka-blue.bio: Poet and teacher at the Rumi Center whose series Mirror of the Infinite teaches Rumi's Masnavi and the Sufi path of the heart.

father-spyridon.bio: Orthodox priest who teaches the Jesus Prayer, repentance and the ascetic teaching of the Fathers in short talks.

angela-puca.bio: Scholar of Western esotericism and magic who runs Angela's Symposium, an academic channel on theurgy, Hermetic magic and the grimoire tradition.

john-main.bio: Irish Benedictine who recovered mantra meditation from John Cassian and the desert tradition; founding inspiration of the WCCM.

moshe-idel.bio: Hebrew University scholar of Kabbalah who reframed the field around ecstatic Kabbalah and Abraham Abulafia.

nimatullahi-order.bio: Official channel of the Nimatullahi order: illustrated classical Sufi teaching stories.

william-rowlandson.bio: Scholar of Borges, Swedenborg and the imaginal who supported the Kent MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

angela-voss.bio: Scholar of Marsilio Ficino and the symbolic imagination who created the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred with Geoffrey Cornelius.

sarah-bachelard.bio: Australian Anglican priest and theologian teaching contemplative Christianity in the WCCM.

becca-tarnas.bio: Scholar of archetypal cosmology, Jung and Tolkien, teaching on the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred diploma.

peter-kingsley.bio: Scholar of the Presocratics who reads Parmenides and Empedocles as mystics and healers, and writes on Jung's Red Book.

tom-cheetham.bio: Philosopher and poet, the leading English-language interpreter of Henry Corbin and of the imaginal in Corbin and Hillman.

seyyed-hossein-nasr.bio: Iranian philosopher of Islam and the perennial philosophy, a leading Traditionalist author and teacher of Chittick.

huston-smith.bio: American scholar of world religions, author of The World's Religions and Forgotten Truth.

james-cutsinger.bio: American scholar of the perennial philosophy and Eastern Orthodox spirituality, editor of Schuon.

james-finley.bio: Clinical psychologist and former Trappist novice under Thomas Merton; CAC faculty and host of Turning to the Mystics.

louise-livingstone.bio: Scholar of the heart and Goethean enquiry, co-founder of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019).

william-chittick.bio: Scholar and translator of Ibn Arabi and Rumi; doctorate at Tehran University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr (1974).

texts.title: Presence with God in Ibn Arabi's Teaching

nazim-al-haqqani.bio: Turkish Cypriot Grand Shaykh of the Naqshbandi-Haqqani order.

geoffrey-cornelius.bio: Astrologer and scholar of divination, co-creator of the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

elliot-wolfson.bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and Jewish philosophy; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis (1986).

daniel-matt.bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and translator of the Pritzker Edition of the Zohar; studied under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis.

prometheus-trust.bio: UK charity founded in 1986 by Tim Addey and others to keep the Platonic tradition alive as a way of life; publisher of the Thomas Taylor Series.

medina-tenour.bio: Teacher on Sufi women saints and nature contemplation at the Rumi Center.

martin-lings.bio: English Sufi author and Shakespeare scholar, disciple of Frithjof Schuon and onetime assistant to René Guénon in Cairo.

rowan-williams.bio: Theologian of Christian spirituality and former Archbishop of Canterbury (2002–2012).

mary-attwood.bio: Art historian of the Renaissance imagination and director of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

william-stoddart.bio: Scottish Traditionalist author on Sufism and the perennial philosophy.

alireza-nurbakhsh.bio: Master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order since 2008, succeeding his father Javad Nurbakhsh.

cyprian-consiglio.bio: Camaldolese monk and musician teaching Christian meditation and interreligious contemplation.

mirabai-starr.bio: Translator of the Spanish mystics and teacher of contemplative practice and grief.

embassy-curators.n: Embassy of the Free Mind curators
embassy-curators.bio: Curators of the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica (Ritman Library) in Amsterdam, giving guided talks on its Hermetic and Böhme collections.

arthur-versluis.bio: American scholar of Western esotericism and mysticism, founding editor of the journal Esoterica and author on Platonic mysticism and Gnosticism.

patrick-curry.bio: Writer on enchantment, divination and ecology who taught on the Kent MA programme.

wouter-hanegraaff.bio: Professor of History of Hermetic Philosophy and Related Currents at the University of Amsterdam and a founder of Western esotericism as an academic field.

simon-wilson.bio: Canterbury Christ Church lecturer and course director of the MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019–2021).

frithjof-schuon.bio: Metaphysician of the transcendent unity of religions and founder of the Maryamiyya Sufi order.

reza-shah-kazemi.bio: Scholar of comparative mysticism and Islamic spirituality.

jean-louis-michon.bio: French scholar of Sufism and Islamic art.

javad-nurbakhsh.bio: Psychiatrist and master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order for 55 years (1953–2008).

bernard-mcginn.bio: University of Chicago historian of Christian mysticism, author of the multi-volume The Presence of God.

christopher-titmuss.bio: British insight meditation teacher, former Thai monk, who co-founded Gaia House in 1983.

christina-feldman.bio: Insight meditation teacher and author who co-founded Gaia House in 1983 and is now one of its patrons.

stephen-batchelor.bio: British former Tibetan and Zen monk, author of secular Buddhist books such as "Buddhism Without Beliefs"; long linked with Gaia House.

martine-batchelor.bio: French former Korean Seon nun and meditation teacher, a patron of Gaia House.

lama-yeshe-losal.bio: Akong Rinpoche's younger brother; retreat master of Samye Ling from 1988 and its abbot since 1995.

jiyu-kennett.bio: English Soto Zen roshi trained at Sojiji who founded Shasta Abbey (1970), Throssel Hole (1972) and the Order of Buddhist Contemplatives.

daishin-morgan.bio: Disciple of Jiyu-Kennett and abbot of Throssel Hole Buddhist Abbey from 1982 to 2019.

ajahn-khemadhammo.bio: English disciple of Ajahn Chah who founded the Forest Hermitage in Warwickshire and the Angulimala prison chaplaincy.

sangharakshita.bio: English monk (Dennis Lingwood) who founded the Triratna Buddhist Community (formerly FWBO) in London in 1967.

img.artist: The original uploader was Tathaataa at English Wikipedia.

pramukh-swami-maharaj.bio: Guru and president of BAPS who inaugurated the Neasden mandir in 1995.

kelsang-gyatso.bio: Tibetan lama who founded the New Kadampa Tradition and its mother centre at Conishead Priory, Cumbria.

sophrony-sakharov.bio: Russian Orthodox elder, disciple and biographer of St Silouan the Athonite, who founded the monastery at Tolleshunt Knights in 1959.

julian-of-norwich.bio: English anchoress whose "Revelations of Divine Love" is the earliest surviving book in English known to be written by a woman.

texts.title: Revelations of Divine Love

george-fox.bio: English dissenter whose preaching from 1652 began the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers).

bulent-rauf.bio: Turkish-born teacher around whom the Beshara School for the study of Ibn 'Arabi formed in the 1970s.

ibn-arabi.bio: Andalusian Sufi master (1165-1240), "the greatest master", whose teaching on the unity of being shaped later Sufism.

inayat-khan.bio: Indian musician and Sufi teacher who brought Sufism to the West, founding his order in London around 1914-1917.

ross-nichols.bio: English poet and teacher who founded the Order of Bards, Ovates and Druids in 1964.

gerald-gardner.bio: English civil servant who publicised the religion of Wicca from the 1950s.

doreen-valiente.bio: English Wiccan priestess and poet, author of much of the Wiccan liturgy including the "Charge of the Goddess".

dion-fortune.bio: British occultist (Violet Firth), founder of the Society (Fraternity) of the Inner Light and author of "The Mystical Qabalah".

img.artist: Author of this photo is unknown person.

aleister-crowley.bio: English occultist, founder of Thelema, initiated in the Golden Dawn; owned Boleskine House.

samuel-liddell-macgregor-mathers.bio: Co-founder of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn (1888) and translator of grimoires.

img.artist: The original uploader was Ihcoyc at English Wikipedia.

emma-restall-orr.bio: English druid and writer who founded The Druid Network.

philip-carr-gomm.bio: Chosen Chief of OBOD from 1988 to 2020, pupil of Ross Nichols.

kathy-jones.bio: Founder of the Glastonbury Goddess Temple and the Glastonbury Goddess Conference.

cecil-williamson.bio: Founder of the Museum of Witchcraft, which settled in Boscastle in 1960.

karl-koenig.bio: Austrian paediatrician who founded the Camphill movement near Aberdeen in 1939-40.

douglas-harding.bio: English philosopher whose "On Having No Head" launched the Headless Way.

christmas-humphreys.bio: English barrister who founded the Buddhist Society in London in 1924.

john-crook.bio: British ethologist and Chan teacher, dharma heir of Sheng Yen, who founded the Western Chan Fellowship.

Iamblichus' Life of Pythagoras

buddhism.label: Buddhism
buddhism.blurb: The path of the Buddha: seeing suffering, its cause in craving, and its ending, through virtue, meditation and wisdom.

theravada.label: Theravāda
theravada.blurb: The oldest surviving Buddhist school, rooted in the Pāli discourses and the monastic code; strong today in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

early-suttas.label: Early suttas
early-suttas.blurb: Practice read straight from the early discourses, outside the commentarial mainstream; Hillside Hermitage belongs here, drawing on Ñāṇavīra Thera.

thai-forest.label: Thai Forest
thai-forest.blurb: The forest monastic lineage of Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah.

insight.label: Insight meditation
insight.blurb: The modern vipassanā movement and its Western retreat centres.

mahayana.label: Mahāyāna
mahayana.blurb: The "great vehicle": the bodhisattva ideal of awakening for the sake of all beings, and the teaching of emptiness.

zen.label: Zen
zen.blurb: Chan and Zen: awakening through sitting, direct pointing and the teacher–student encounter, more than through scripture.

vajrayana.label: Vajrayāna
vajrayana.blurb: Tantric Buddhism: deity practice, mantra and the teacher's transmission as a swift path to awakening.

tibetan.label: Tibetan Buddhism
tibetan.blurb: The Buddhism of the Himalaya, joining monastic study and debate with Vajrayāna practice and guidance for the dying.

hindu.label: Hindu traditions
hindu.blurb: The many paths that grew from the Vedas and Upanishads: knowledge, devotion, yoga and action.

vedanta.label: Vedānta
vedanta.blurb: Philosophy built on the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gītā and the Brahma Sūtras, asking how the self relates to Brahman.

advaita.label: Advaita Vedānta
advaita.blurb: Non-dual Vedānta: the Self (ātman) is Brahman, and the world of separate selves is an appearance.

inchegeri.label: Inchegeri Sampradaya
inchegeri.blurb: The Navnath line of Siddharameshwar and Nisargadatta Maharaj.

ramakrishna-order.label: Ramakrishna Order
ramakrishna-order.blurb: The monastic order founded on Ramakrishna's teaching and Vivekananda's mission: Vedānta lived as service.

kashmir-shaivism.label: Kashmir Shaivism
kashmir-shaivism.blurb: A non-dual Tantric philosophy in which the world is the free, conscious play of Shiva, recognised as one's own self.

kriya-yoga.label: Kriya Yoga
kriya-yoga.blurb: The line of Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya and Paramahansa Yogananda.

christian.label: Christian traditions
christian.blurb: The traditions that follow Jesus of Nazareth, from the Gospels and the early Church to the mystics.

christian-mysticism.label: Christian mysticism
christian-mysticism.blurb: Christians who sought direct union with God: detachment, contemplative prayer and the birth of God in the soul.

gnosticism.label: Gnosticism
gnosticism.blurb: Early Christian and related movements of saving knowledge (gnosis); known mostly through texts such as the Nag Hammadi library.

platonic.label: Platonic tradition
platonic.blurb: Philosophy as the care of the soul, turning from the world of change toward the eternal Forms and the Good.

neoplatonism.label: Neoplatonism
neoplatonism.blurb: Late antique Platonism: everything flows from the One, and the soul can return to it through contemplation.

renaissance-platonism.label: Renaissance Platonism
renaissance-platonism.blurb: The revival of Plato and Plotinus in fifteenth-century Florence, joining Platonic philosophy with Christian faith.

esoteric.label: Western esotericism
esoteric.blurb: Western paths of hidden knowledge: Hermeticism, Theosophy, Anthroposophy and the Fourth Way.

theosophy.label: Theosophy
theosophy.blurb: The movement of Blavatsky and the Theosophical Society, joining Eastern ideas of karma and rebirth with Western occultism.

anthroposophy.label: Anthroposophy
anthroposophy.blurb: Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science: a path of clear thinking toward knowledge of spiritual worlds, karma and repeated earth lives.

fourth-way.label: The Fourth Way
fourth-way.blurb: Gurdjieff's path of self-remembering and conscious effort in the middle of ordinary life.

independent.label: Independent
independent.blurb: Teachers who stand outside any tradition.

direct-path.label: Direct path
direct-path.blurb: The non-dual enquiry into experience taught by Atmananda Krishna Menon and carried on by Jean Klein, Francis Lucille and Rupert Spira.

arsha-vidya.label: Arsha Vidya
arsha-vidya.blurb: Traditional teaching of Advaita Vedanta through the texts, in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Q4796497).

modern-nondual.label: Modern non-dual teachers
modern-nondual.blurb: Contemporary teachers of awakening who draw on Zen, Advaita and other sources without belonging to one lineage.

plum-village.label: Plum Village
plum-village.blurb: Thich Nhat Hanh's Vietnamese Thiền community of engaged, mindful living.

soto-zen.label: Sōtō Zen
soto-zen.blurb: Dōgen's school of just-sitting (shikantaza); San Francisco Zen Center, Sanshin.

rinzai-zen.label: Rinzai Zen
rinzai-zen.blurb: The koan school of Japanese Zen; Zen Studies Society.

gelug.label: Gelug
gelug.blurb: The Tibetan school of Tsongkhapa, headed in practice by the Dalai Lamas.

burmese.label: Burmese meditation lineages
burmese.blurb: Myanmar's modern meditation schools: Mahasi noting, Pa-Auk samatha-vipassanā, U Ba Khin and Goenka.

krishnamurti.label: Krishnamurti
krishnamurti.blurb: J. Krishnamurti's teaching after he left Theosophy in 1929: no path, no authority, freedom from the known.

anandamayi-sangha.label: Anandamayi Ma Sangha
anandamayi-sangha.blurb: The ashrams and monastics around Anandamayi Ma (Shree Shree Anandamayee Sangha, Kankhal and Varanasi), devotional and non-sectarian.

divine-life-society.label: Divine Life Society
divine-life-society.blurb: The order founded by Swami Sivananda in Rishikesh, carried on by Swami Chidananda.

siddha-yoga.label: Siddha Yoga
siddha-yoga.blurb: Guru-yoga path founded by Swami Muktananda in the line of Bhagawan Nityananda: shaktipat, chanting and meditation, drawing on Kashmir Shaiva texts.

goenka-vipassana.label: Goenka Vipassana (U Ba Khin line)
goenka-vipassana.blurb: Lay Vipassana in the line of Ledi Sayadaw, Saya Thetgyi and U Ba Khin, taught by S. N. Goenka in 10-day dana-funded courses.

kagyu.label: Kagyu
kagyu.blurb: Tibetan school of the mahamudra lineage from Tilopa and Naropa through Marpa and Milarepa, led by the Karmapas.

nyingma.label: Nyingma
nyingma.blurb: The oldest Tibetan school, tracing to Padmasambhava, home of Dzogchen.

sufism.label: Sufism
sufism.blurb: The inner, mystical path of Islam: remembrance of God (dhikr), the master and the order, the poetry of love.

jewish.label: Jewish mysticism
jewish.blurb: Merkavah, Kabbalah, the Zohar and Hasidism: the contemplative and mystical currents of Judaism.

philosophy-of-the-sacred.label: Philosophy of the sacred
philosophy-of-the-sacred.blurb: Contemporary philosophers and scientists on consciousness, meaning and the sacred: idealism, the divided brain, the meaning crisis, perennialism.

modern-paganism.label: Modern Paganism
modern-paganism.blurb: Druidry, Wicca, Heathenry and goddess spirituality: nature-centred traditions revived or founded in the modern era.

sikh.label: Sikhism
sikh.blurb: The path of the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib: remembrance of the one Name, honest work and sharing.

shaivism.label: Śaivism
shaivism.blurb: Umbrella for Śiva-centred traditions: the ascetic Atimārga and the initiatory Mantramārga.

pashupata.label: Pāśupata (Atimārga)
pashupata.blurb: Earliest Śaiva ascetic order; ash, feigned madness, provoking censure.

shaiva-siddhanta.label: Śaiva Siddhānta
shaiva-siddhanta.blurb: Mainstream ritual Śaivism of the Mantramārga; Sanskrit āgamas, later the Tamil Śaiva temple tradition. Kauai Aadheenam teaches a monistic form.

trika.label: Trika
trika.blurb: Abhinavagupta's synthesis around the Mālinīvijayottara; Tantrāloka.

pratyabhijna.label: Pratyabhijñā (Recognition)
pratyabhijna.blurb: Philosophical school: liberation as recognising oneself as Śiva.

spanda.label: Spanda (Vibration)
spanda.blurb: Śiva Sūtras and Spanda Kārikās: consciousness as pulsation.

krama.label: Krama / Kālīkula (Mahārtha)
krama.blurb: Kālī-centred phases (krama) of cognition; Twelve Kālīs.

shaktism.label: Śāktism
shaktism.blurb: Goddess-centred traditions; parent of Kaula, Śrī Vidyā and Kālī lines.

shakta.label: Śākta practice (Kālī, Kāmākhyā, Bhairavī)
shakta.blurb: Bucket for living goddess practice not tied to a single classical school (Kāmākhyā upāsanā, Linga Bhairavi, Daśa Mahāvidyā).

sri-vidya.label: Śrī Vidyā
sri-vidya.blurb: Worship of Lalitā Tripurasundarī through the Śrī Chakra and the fifteen-syllable mantra.

siddha-siddhanta.label: Nāth / Siddha Siddhānta
siddha-siddhanta.blurb: Nāth yogī order (Gorakhnāth); Siddha Siddhānta Paddhati; alchemy and haṭha.

hatha.label: Haṭha Yoga (premodern)
hatha.blurb: Physical-yogic methods first set out in Vajrayāna and Śaiva circles (Amṛtasiddhi, Dattātreyayogaśāstra, Haṭhapradīpikā).

tantra-studies.label: Tantra studies (academic)
tantra-studies.blurb: Not a tradition: a field tag for scholarly lectures (philology, history).

chah-line.label: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)
chah-line.blurb: Includes Amaravati, Chithurst/Cittaviveka, Abhayagiri, Bodhinyana/BSWA, Wat Pah Nanachat, Wat Marp Jan, Wat Boonyawad, Tisarana, Birken.

mun-boowa-line.label: Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)
mun-boowa-line.blurb: Note: Ajahn Dtun, listed by the brief under this line, was ordained by Ajahn Chah (Mahānikāya) and is filed under chah-line.

pa-auk.label: Pa-Auk (samatha-first, Abhidhamma)
pa-auk.blurb: No usable official English short talks found this pass.

mogok.label: Mogok Sayadaw (dependent origination)
mogok.blurb: Official channel is Burmese-language only; no English clips.

sri-lankan.label: Sri Lankan Theravāda (forest & scholastic)
sri-lankan.blurb: Hillside Hermitage is already deep in app (early-suttas).

buddhist-studies.label: Buddhist studies (academic)
buddhist-studies.blurb: Scholarly lineage node: edges are academic_supervisor_of.

sivananda-yoga.label: Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
sivananda-yoga.blurb: Swami Vishnudevananda's international centres teaching his guru Sivananda's yoga.

bihar-yoga.label: Bihar School of Yoga (Satyananda Yoga)
bihar-yoga.blurb: Yoga of Swami Satyananda, disciple of Sivananda, and the Bihar School of Yoga.

gaudiya.label: Gaudiya Vaishnava (Chaitanya / ISKCON)
gaudiya.blurb: Krishna devotion in the line of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

dzogchen.label: Dzogchen (Great Perfection)
dzogchen.blurb: Teaching and practice lineage, not a separate institution; also held in Bön and taught across Rimé.

karma-kagyu.label: Karma Kagyu
karma-kagyu.blurb: Largest Kagyu branch, led by the Karmapas.

shangpa-kagyu.label: Shangpa Kagyu
shangpa-kagyu.blurb: Separate lineage from Niguma and Sukhasiddhi, revived by Kalu Rinpoche.

mahamudra.label: Mahamudra (the Great Seal)
mahamudra.blurb: Practice lineage at the heart of Kagyu, also taught in Gelug.

sakya.label: Sakya
sakya.blurb: Lamdre (path and its fruit) teachings; led by the Khön family.

fpmt.label: FPMT (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition)
fpmt.blurb: International Gelug network founded by Lama Yeshe and Lama Zopa.

jonang.label: Jonang
jonang.blurb: Known for shentong (other-emptiness) and Kalachakra; suppressed in central Tibet in the 17th c. and survives in Amdo.

bon.label: Bön (Yungdrung Bön)
bon.blurb: Tibet's indigenous religion. It is not a Buddhist school, but it shares its institutions and Dzogchen with Buddhism. Placed here for browsing only.

rime.label: Rimé (non-sectarian) movement
rime.blurb: An ecumenical revival across Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Jonang, not a school.

shambhala.label: Shambhala
shambhala.blurb: Trungpa's secular "warrior" path; Pema Chödrön trained in it.

chan.label: Chan
chan.blurb: Chinese meditation school, root of Zen, Seon and Thiền.

dharma-drum.label: Dharma Drum Mountain
dharma-drum.blurb: Taiwanese Chan organisation of Sheng Yen holding both Linji and Caodong lines.

sanbo-zen.label: Sanbo Zen (Sanbo Kyodan)
sanbo-zen.blurb: Lay-oriented school combining Soto and Rinzai koan curricula.

white-plum.label: White Plum Asanga
white-plum.blurb: Maezumi's lineage network (Soto with Rinzai koan study).

seon.label: Seon (Korean Zen)
seon.blurb: Korean Chan; Jogye order; Kwan Um School in the West.

kwan-um.label: Kwan Um School of Zen
kwan-um.blurb: International Seon school of Seung Sahn.

plum-village-thien.label: Thiền
plum-village-thien.blurb: Vietnamese Chan; Plum Village is its best-known modern form.

ocb.label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives
ocb.blurb: Shasta Abbey tradition founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

tiantai.label: Tiantai
tiantai.blurb: Lotus Sutra school; threefold truth; zhiguan (calming and contemplation).

tendai.label: Tendai
tendai.blurb: Japanese Tiantai, which also includes esoteric (taimitsu), Pure Land and Zen elements.

huayan.label: Huayan (Kegon)
huayan.blurb: Avatamsaka school; interpenetration of all phenomena.

pure-land.label: Pure Land
pure-land.blurb: Devotion to Amitabha and rebirth in Sukhavati.

jodo-shinshu.label: Jōdo Shinshū (Shin Buddhism)
jodo-shinshu.blurb: Shinran's school; Buddhist Churches of America in the US.

east-asian-esoteric.label: East Asian esoteric Buddhism
east-asian-esoteric.blurb: Chinese Zhenyan and its Japanese heirs.

western-magic.label: Western magic
western-magic.blurb: Ritual and initiatory magic in the Hermetic and Qabalistic line: the Golden Dawn, Thelema, the Inner Light.

akbarian.label: Akbarian school (Ibn Arabi)
akbarian.blurb: Study and practice centred on Ibn 'Arabi's teaching of the unity of being, as at Beshara.

naqshbandi.label: Naqshbandi-Haqqani order
naqshbandi.blurb: Sufi order known for silent remembrance (dhikr) and tracing its chain through Abu Bakr.

inayati.label: Inayatiyya (universal Sufism, Chishti roots)
inayati.blurb: Universal Sufism of Hazrat Inayat Khan, founded in London around 1914-1917.

christian-meditation-wccm.label: Christian Meditation (John Main / WCCM)
christian-meditation-wccm.blurb: Contemplative prayer with a single prayer word, taught by John Main and the World Community for Christian Meditation.

franciscan.label: Franciscan contemplative (Rohr / CAC)
franciscan.blurb: Followers of St Francis; in the UK including the Anglican Society of St Francis.

hesychasm.label: Orthodox hesychasm
hesychasm.blurb: Eastern Orthodox prayer of inner stillness and the Jesus Prayer.

kabbalah.label: Kabbalah (theosophical and ecstatic)
kabbalah.blurb: Jewish mystical tradition of the sefirot and the hidden meanings of Torah; also its modern popular forms.

druidry.label: Druidry
druidry.blurb: Modern Druid spirituality of nature, the seasonal festivals and bardic arts, as in OBOD.

wicca.label: Wicca
wicca.blurb: Modern pagan witchcraft publicised by Gerald Gardner from the 1950s, with covens, the Goddess and God and the wheel of the year.

heathenry.label: Heathenry
heathenry.blurb: Modern revival of pre-Christian Germanic and Norse religion (Asatru, Odinism).

goddess-spirituality.label: Goddess spirituality
goddess-spirituality.blurb: Devotion to the divine feminine as Goddess, centred in the UK on Glastonbury.

golden-dawn.label: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
golden-dawn.blurb: Initiatory order founded in London in 1888 that shaped modern Western magic.

thelema.label: Thelema
thelema.blurb: Aleister Crowley's religious and magical system ("Do what thou wilt").

quaker.label: Quakers (Religious Society of Friends)
quaker.blurb: Christian movement begun by George Fox in 1652, worshipping in expectant silence.

benedictine.label: Benedictine monasticism
benedictine.blurb: Monastic life under the Rule of St Benedict.

cistercian.label: Cistercians (Trappists)
cistercian.blurb: Reformed Benedictines; Trappists are the Strict Observance.

carmelite.label: Carmelites
carmelite.blurb: Contemplative order of Teresa of Avila and John of the Cross.

ignatian.label: Ignatian spirituality
ignatian.blurb: The Jesuit way of the Spiritual Exercises of Ignatius of Loyola.

celtic-christianity.label: Celtic Christianity
celtic-christianity.blurb: The early Christianity of Britain and Ireland (Columba, Aidan, Cuthbert, David) and its modern revival.

triratna.label: Triratna Buddhist Community
triratna.blurb: Western Buddhist movement founded by Sangharakshita in London in 1967 (formerly FWBO).

new-kadampa.label: New Kadampa Tradition
new-kadampa.blurb: Movement founded by Kelsang Gyatso in England, presenting itself as independent of the Tibetan schools (Gelug-derived; contested).

serene-reflection.label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives (Serene Reflection)
serene-reflection.blurb: Soto Zen order founded by Jiyu-Kennett, seated at Shasta Abbey and Throssel Hole.

nipponzan-myohoji.label: Nipponzan-Myohoji
nipponzan-myohoji.blurb: Japanese Nichiren order of Nichidatsu Fujii that builds peace pagodas.

iskcon.label: ISKCON (Hare Krishna)
iskcon.blurb: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, founded by A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in 1966.

swaminarayan.label: Swaminarayan Sampradaya
swaminarayan.blurb: Vaishnava tradition of Swaminarayan, including BAPS.

brahma-kumaris.label: Brahma Kumaris
brahma-kumaris.blurb: Spiritual movement founded in Sindh in the 1930s, teaching Raja Yoga meditation; headquarters at Mount Abu.

transcendental-meditation.label: Transcendental Meditation
transcendental-meditation.blurb: Mantra meditation of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi.

swedenborgian.label: Swedenborgianism
swedenborgian.blurb: Thought and church following the visions of Emanuel Swedenborg.

spiritualism.label: Spiritualism
spiritualism.blurb: Movement based on communication with the dead through mediums.

kaula.label: Kaula / Kula
kaula.blurb: Clan (kula) cults of yoginīs and Bhairava; source of many later Śākta and haṭha practices.

takes.theravada: Craving and kamma drive a new birth, yet no unchanging self passes from life to life.
takes.tibetan: Between death and the next birth lies the bardo, where the mind meets its own nature and its habits.
takes.vedanta: The subtle body moves from life to life, carried by karma; the Self you are was never born and never dies.
takes.platonic: The soul is immortal and returns to new lives, choosing its next life by what it has become (the Myth of Er).
takes.anthroposophy: The human I returns through repeated earth lives, meeting the karma it has made and growing through it.
takes.krishnamurti: Asks what it is that would be reborn: the stream of memory called the self can end now, which matters more than a next life.

takes.theravada: Kamma is intention: what you will and do shapes what you meet and who you become.
takes.tibetan: Actions ripen across lives; purification and merit change how they ripen, and wisdom uproots them.
takes.vedanta: Action binds as long as it is done for its fruits; action offered without attachment frees.
takes.kashmir-shaivism: Karma is one of the three impurities that veil consciousness; recognising your nature as Śiva dissolves it.
takes.kriya-yoga: Right action and meditation work out past karma; Kriya practice is taught as a way to hasten it.
takes.anthroposophy: Karma is a just weaving of destiny across lives, worked out in the meetings and trials of each new life.
takes.fourth-way: Most of what we call action is mechanical; only conscious effort is truly ours.

takes.theravada: Nothing you can point to as yours is a lasting self; seeing this ends the conceit 'I am'.
takes.zen: Study the self to forget the self: the self, like all things, has no fixed essence apart from everything else.
takes.tibetan: The self is empty of inherent existence; it exists only as a label placed on body and mind.
takes.vedanta: Ask 'Who am I?': under every thought is the one Self, pure awareness, which is Brahman.
takes.kashmir-shaivism: The self is Śiva, free consciousness; awakening is recognising what you already are.
takes.christian-mysticism: Let go of the self that clings, and God is found in the ground of the soul.
takes.fourth-way: We have no single permanent I, only many passing 'I's; a real I has to be built through work on oneself.
takes.krishnamurti: The self is a bundle of memory and reaction; to see it clearly, without a watcher, is freedom.

takes.theravada: Recollect death daily: it loosens clinging and shows the urgency of the path.
takes.zen: Birth and death are the life of the way itself; seen clearly, they lose their grip on the mind.
takes.tibetan: Death is a doorway: rightly prepared, the moment of dying can be the moment of liberation.
takes.vedanta: Death belongs to the body and the mind; find out who it is that fears it.
takes.platonic: Philosophy is practice for dying: the soul's training in turning from the body toward what is real.
takes.anthroposophy: After death the soul looks back on its life, is purified (kamaloca) and prepares for a new birth.
takes.krishnamurti: Die each day to what you know and hold; then death is not at the far end of life but within it.

takes.theravada: Restraint and right view first; then the mind settles and sees the arising and passing of things.
takes.zen: Just sit: practice is not a means to awakening but its expression.
takes.tibetan: Calm the mind, then recognise its nature: awareness itself, open and clear.
takes.vedanta: Quiet the mind through discipline or devotion, then rest as the awareness in which all experience comes and goes.
takes.kashmir-shaivism: Practices such as those of the Vijñāna Bhairava turn any moment of experience back to the consciousness it arises in.
takes.kriya-yoga: Breath and life-energy techniques still the mind and turn it inward, toward the divine.
takes.christian-mysticism: Contemplative prayer: rest in God beyond words and images.
takes.fourth-way: Self-remembering: be present to yourself in the middle of ordinary life.
takes.krishnamurti: Not a method but choiceless awareness: watching the movement of thought without a controller.

takes.theravada: Nibbāna is the ending of greed, hatred and delusion, reached through stages that cannot be lost.
takes.zen: Awakening is seeing your own nature, sudden or gradual, and then living it.
takes.tibetan: Buddhahood is the full recognition of the mind's own nature, wisdom and compassion inseparable.
takes.vedanta: Liberation is not gained; it is the end of the mistaken belief that you were ever bound.
takes.kashmir-shaivism: Liberation is recognition (pratyabhijñā): you have always been Śiva, free consciousness.
takes.neoplatonism: The soul turns inward and ascends until it is one with the One.
takes.christian-mysticism: Union with God, reached through love and letting go, in which the soul finds God in its own ground.
takes.fourth-way: We are asleep; waking up begins with seeing our own mechanicalness and remembering ourselves.

takes.theravada: Craving is the origin of suffering; when it fades, suffering ends.
takes.zen: Desire is met with open attention rather than fought; seen as empty, it loosens by itself.
takes.vedanta: Desire for the fruits of action keeps the wheel turning; the longing for liberation is the one desire worth keeping.
takes.platonic: Desire is redirected, not destroyed: love rises from beautiful things toward Beauty itself.
takes.christian-mysticism: Detachment: want nothing but God, and the soul is free.

takes.theravada: Life as we grasp it is unsatisfying; see its cause and it can end.
takes.zen: Suffering is met, not escaped: held in mindful attention, it can be transformed.
takes.tibetan: Suffering comes from grasping at a self; seeing others suffer as we do is the root of compassion.
takes.vedanta: Suffering comes from taking yourself to be the body and mind.
takes.christian: Suffering can be carried and transformed, in communion with Christ's own.
takes.krishnamurti: Sorrow ends when you meet it completely, without escaping into explanation.
